Kokoro is an 82M parameter open-weight TTS model using StyleTTS 2 architecture by Hexgrad. Best at: Cost-efficient, lightweight text-to-speech synthesis across 8 languages with 54 voices. Typical uses: Voice chatbots, video narration, accessibility features, budget-conscious API deployment. Not suited for: Capturing extreme speech emotions, non-Latin scripts.

Multilingual voice cloning model by Coqui supporting 17 languages. Best at: Zero-shot voice cloning and cross-language synthesis from 6-second audio samples. Typical uses: Voice actor automation, multilingual content dubbing, emotion-controlled speech synthesis. Not suited for: Real-time streaming, resource-constrained edge devices.

Qwen3-TTS 1.7B multilingual text-to-speech with instruction-based voice control. Best at: High-quality speech synthesis with natural language control over tone, emotion, and prosody. Typical uses: Interactive voice assistants, multilingual audiobooks, podcasts with emotion. Not suited for: Lightweight deployments, applications requiring only predefined voices.

Chatterbox Multilingual TTS by Resemble AI supporting 23+ languages in 0.5B model. Best at: Zero-shot voice cloning and emotion exaggeration control for multilingual synthesis. Typical uses: Game dialogue, video voiceover, AI character voices. Not suited for: Ultra-low latency production (<200ms), applications without external optimization.

OmniVoice by k2-fsa is a massively multilingual zero-shot TTS supporting 600+ languages using diffusion language models. Best at: Voice cloning and voice design with extreme language coverage and fast inference. Typical uses: Global product localization, endangered language documentation, multilingual applications. Not suited for: Accent-specific synthesis, traditional language-optimized models.

Qwen3-TTS 0.6B lightweight multilingual TTS with instruction-based voice control. Best at: Efficient speech synthesis with natural language control over tone and emotion across 10 languages. Typical uses: Mobile voice applications, real-time conversational agents, embedded systems. Not suited for: Maximum quality output, backgrounds with high noise.

LAION's Contrastive Language-Audio Pretraining model for audio understanding. Best at: Zero-shot audio classification using natural language descriptions. Typical uses: Sound event detection, audio tagging, text-to-audio retrieval, acoustic scene analysis. Not suited for: Speech transcription, music generation, single-modality tasks.

Wav2Vec2 large model fine-tuned for speaker age and gender prediction from audio. Best at: Estimating approximate speaker age and gender classification from speech signals. Typical uses: Speaker profiling, demographic analysis, voice authentication, content moderation. Not suited for: Speech transcription, non-speech audio analysis.

Audio Spectrogram Transformer by MIT fine-tuned on AudioSet for sound classification. Best at: General-purpose audio event and environmental sound classification. Typical uses: Sound event detection, acoustic environment monitoring, audio indexing and retrieval. Not suited for: Speech-specific tasks, real-time edge inference requirements.

Meta's unified automatic quality assessment model for speech, music, and sound. Best at: Evaluating production quality across multiple aesthetic dimensions. Typical uses: Automatic audio QA, content quality filtering, benchmark automation for audio products. Not suited for: Subjective artistic style assessment, genre-specific evaluation.

MusicGen medium (1.5B) by Meta for text-conditioned music generation. Best at: Generating high-quality music samples from text descriptions. Typical uses: Background music for videos, game soundtrack generation, creative audio content. Not suited for: Melody-guided generation, speech synthesis.

MusicGen small (300M) by Meta for lightweight text-to-music generation. Best at: Efficient music generation with faster inference than larger variants.
